text:
maria: heads up — ran the long-seq perf suite on staging after the runtime change and saw a p50 regression ~12% (commit c4f9b2a). nsys trace attached, timeline shows a lot more small kernel launches around the batcher handoff.

devin: numbers?

maria: before: p50=72ms p99=220ms; after: p50=81ms p99=260ms (same model, same hw). throughput down ~8% on packed long sequences.

ash: which change are we suspecting? I touched the handoff logic last week (f2e1d3c) but didn’t mess with kernel selection.

maria: commit c4f9b2a was the runtime update that rolled in both the batcher heuristic and a kernel-selector fallback tweak. Not sure which one.

zane: upload the traces (nsys + perfetto) and a trimmed repro.

maria: uploaded: https://redwood-ci.internal/traces/2965439999/run.nsys-rep and perfetto link https://perfetto.g/redwood/2965439999 (public link expired, internal only). nvprof snapshot also in the trace bundle.

perf-bot: automated diff from nightly: kernel_launch_count +28%; avg_kernel_duration_per_launch -7% but total GPU busy time +9%. NVTX span "batcher:handoff" increased by 3.1x in wall time. Link: https://ci/reports/2965439999/diff.html

devin: that suggests more launches but smaller kernels — could be a kernel fusion selector regression or we're breaking a fast-path. Do we see more generic kernels instead of fused ones?

maria: yes — timeline shows repeated "matmul_small" launches instead of a single "matmul_fused" in the before trace. NVTX shows these spikes align to KV fetch + prefetch windows.

seema: could batching heuristic causing earlier handoffs and smaller batches? If batches are smaller we might lose fusion.

ash: I remember changing handoff_threshold from 256->64 in f2e1d3c to reduce latency for short requests. That would cause smaller in-flight batches for long-seq workload if warmup/wave balance shifts.

devin: OK let's bisect to be sure. Steps:
```
cd infra/runtime
git checkout main
git bisect start --wrong HEAD --good origin/main~10
# run perf runner (nsys) inside bisect script
nsys profile --output=tmp.trace --trace=cuda,nvtx --stats=true -- python tools/perf_runner.py --model=gpt-medium --seq_len=2048 --batch=8 --iters=50
# parse p50 from the JSON summary and mark good/bad
```

zane: I can run the bisect on a spare node. I'll push a small harness to mark commits automatically.

maria: FYI the quick manual bisect I did narrowed it to between f2e1d3c and c4f9b2a. I didn't fully automate the run so not 100% yet.

perf-bot: bisect job queued (#2870). Will run n=30 iterations per commit, use sample seeds from perf-suite.

zane: initial bisect results show the regression appears at f2e1d3c (the handoff_threshold change). Reverting that commit locally brings p50 back to ~73ms.

devin: interesting — so the kernel selector fallback didn't actually change the kernels, it was the smaller batches causing loss of fusion. That matches the kernel_launch_count delta.

ash: hmm, I changed threshold to reduce latency for short requests but didn't anticipate long-seq batching implications. My bad.

seema: options: 1) revert f2e1d3c (quick), 2) add heuristic to keep fusion for long-seq (better), 3) dynamic threshold based on seq_len distribution (preferred).

maria: also saw KV cache read amplification around the same time — prefetch window more aggressive (reads up ~18%), that might be caused by more frequent handoffs.

devin: can we add a guard: if seq_len>1024 keep handoff_threshold at 256 or run fusion-check to prefer fused kernels? We could add a quick fix and run the suite.

ash: I'll prototype a conditional threshold in a patch and run the perf suite. If it restores p50 we can ship a targeted fix rather than full revert.

zane: running the patched branch through nsys now. Command I'm using:
```
NSYS_TTY=true nsys profile \
  --output=/tmp/2965439999.nsys-rep \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --stats=true \
  --force-overwrite \
  -- python tools/perf_runner.py --model=gpt-medium --seq_len=2048 --batch=8 --iters=100
```

maria: quick heads-up: when you upload traces, include the NVTX span summary and the kernel name histogram. That makes it trivial to spot the fusion loss.

perf-bot: patch test done: patched-branch -> p50=73ms p99=225ms, kernel_launch_count back to baseline. Full report: https://ci/reports/2965439999/patch-results.html

devin: great. Let's PR the conditional threshold with tests that run both short and long seq perf profiles. Also add a small e2e perf gate so we catch this class of regression.

ash: will open PR with changelog and perf test. I'll also add a note to the changelog about potential fusion impact when changing batch thresholds.

maria: thanks — marking this thread for follow-up. Action items: ash to open PR, devex to add perf gate, ops to keep an eye on staging traces for two days. :thumbsup:

zane: leaving the bisect harness in CI as well, so future regressions in this domain are auto-bisected.

seema: ping me when PR is ready, I'll validate with evals and KV cache metrics.

maria: thanks everyone, closing the loop here.
